svg.aria-label: Three-panel structural geology sheet. Panel A defines strike and dip on a tilted bed in a block diagram and shows the matching map symbol. Panel B shows an anticline and syncline cut by an erosion surface, with the oldest unit exposed in the anticline core and the youngest in the syncline core, and the mirrored map pattern beneath. Panel C shows normal, thrust and strike-slip faults with the vertical principal stress marked for each and their map symbols.
svg.text: A · Strike and dip: two numbers fix a plane in space
strike = the horizontal line in the plane; dip = the steepest angle down from horizontal,
measured in the vertical plane perpendicular to strike. Every other line in the plane is shallower.
B · Erode a fold and the map tells you the stress
map view of the erosion surface
pattern: 3 2 1 2 3 4 5 4 3 — a mirror about each hinge
limbs dip AWAY from the hinge;
the YOUNGEST unit sits in the core.
Dips reverse across each hinge and
the section repeats as a mirror.
A thrust also repeats section, but
in the SAME order with dips
unchanged — that is how you tell
a fold from a thrust on a map.
C · Which principal stress is vertical names the fault
dip about 30 deg; older on younger
σ2 vertical; σ1 at 30 deg to fault
